holidays.name: National Miniature Golf Day
holidays.description: Grab a colorful ball and a pint-sized putter. Today is for windmills, tiny castles, loop-the-loops and the thrill of a hole-in-one on a hole shaped like a clown's mouth.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that celebrates putt-putt fun. The pastime itself goes back more than a century. An early American miniature course was built in Pinehurst, North Carolina, in 1916. Garnet Carter later patented and popularized the Tom Thumb Golf style in the late 1920s.
holidays.funFact: In the late 1920s, miniature golf became so popular in the U.S. that thousands of courses popped up, including some on rooftops.

holidays.name: National Pecan Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day to honor buttery, nutty cookies. Think pecan sandies, crunchy pecan shortbread and chewy pecan-studded treats, all best eaten with a cold glass of milk.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It gives cookie lovers a reason to bake with one of North America's native nuts.
holidays.funFact: The pecan is native to North America, and its name comes from an Algonquian word for nuts that need a stone to crack them.

holidays.name: National Chai Day
holidays.description: Time to sip the spiced, milky tea that warms hands and hearts. Brew it with cardamom, cinnamon, ginger and cloves, and feel free to argue about the right recipe.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the spiced tea tradition of India, which has spread around the world.
holidays.funFact: In Hindi, the word chai simply means tea. Saying chai tea is like saying tea tea.
